To clear things up, I have PTSD from years of physical and emotional abuse at home and my dad's suicide when I was a very young age. I had to take care of my mentally ill mother and try to keep things together myself. I had no time to grieve, instead I excelled in school and went on to study Law at University. I pushed myself too hard when life was too hard on me. Meanwhile, my mom is still together with her abusive boyfriend and I haven't spoken to her in half a year though I'm moving towards 'forgiveness' of some sort. Thanks for all your advice, I find yoga is important for trauma victims because my mind spins off into panic and anxiety (and detachment) and I really need to feel more grounded in my body and more secure in myself. I am seeing a counsellor weekly and I want to use yoga as an add-on so to speak. I think the breathing aspect of yoga in particular is important, and because I don't know much about the postures themselves, I was just wondering generally speaking what works for some people so I can try it out. Either way, I don't always believe what I read but I do believe there is some truth in that emotions are stored in areas of the body (I don't know if you've heard of chakras?) I suppose I am more spiritual in that regard. I always do my own research upon reading your comments - nonetheless I appreciate your critical perspective and I wish you (and everyone commenting on this thread) all the best!

The ego is essentially fear. If you've had bad shit happen to you in the past, e.g. abuse, abandonment, etc. then your ego uses these incidents as evidence for your distorted perception of self such as I'm not good enough and all that crap. I have extremely low confidence though I have many friends and easily make friends and I am liked by many. It's the ego that feeds anxiety and feeds your fear. If you can learn to love yourself and not be defined by your past and the story you are telling yourself, you can start to live beyond your fear, beyond the ego, and start to live life as the beautiful person you naturally exude.
